name: product-feature-registry
purpose: Defines the installable desktop product as an agent capability platform whose primary value is orchestration, agent work, development, creation, and continuous improvement. Monitoring is only a supporting observability layer.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry before changing the desktop home screen, snapshot schema, installer shell runtime, or platform feature navigation.
how_to_read: Read product_position first to understand what the product is and what it is not.
Read feature_layers to see which capabilities are primary product features and which capabilities are supporting surfaces.
Read promotion_loop before adding workflow, prompt, tool, skill, or agent creation features.
Read structure_rules before naming a feature, tab, data store, or installer shell behavior as monitoring.
Use validation_gates as the acceptance checklist when making a UI, data, or runtime change around these features.
update_triggers: The desktop home screen or first-run product promise changes.
A feature is promoted from workflow, prompt, template, tool, skill, or agent into a desktop product surface.
A new agent orchestration, workbench, development, factory, learning, or observability capability is added.
Monitoring starts to look like the main product again instead of a support layer.
The installer shell runtime contract changes how work state, decisions, evidence, validation, or evaluations are accumulated.

structure_rules.rule: The desktop product shall be positioned as an agent capability platform, not as a monitoring dashboard.
structure_rules.reason: The user explicitly rejected a UI that keeps behaving like a web monitor or PoC.

structure_rules.rule: Existing shell, source review, runtime data, decision inbox, history, requirements, and monitoring pieces shall be surfaced as named product features with a clear primary or supporting role.
structure_rules.reason: The product should stop scattering surfaces as implementation leftovers and should expose them as sellable feature modules.

structure_rules.rule: Monitoring, history browsing, structure browsing, document browsing, requirements browsing, and diagnostic views shall support orchestration, workbench, development, factory, and learning features; they shall not become the product's main promise.
structure_rules.reason: The user said monitoring is not the main function and current UI choices were blocking correct product decisions.

structure_rules.rule: Operator, monitoring, document, requirement, project registry, and structure surfaces shall live behind a dedicated Operator Center or settings-style surface instead of the primary work navigation.
structure_rules.reason: A sellable desktop app should foreground agent work and keep admin/review surfaces available without making them feel like the product.

structure_rules.rule: Agent creation, capability promotion, evaluation, work history, and improvement records shall be designed as a continuous product loop, not as static documentation.
structure_rules.reason: The product must make agents easier to create and continuously improve through accumulated data.

structure_rules.rule: Configuration and setup should be handled through dedicated settings, capability, or modal surfaces instead of being spread across one dashboard screen.
structure_rules.reason: A desktop app should separate work execution, configuration, and review surfaces like mature desktop tools do.

structure_rules.rule: Already defined agents shall be exposed as runnable desktop product surfaces before asking the user to create another agent.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked to easily run the existing search agent instead of hunting through configs or shell commands.

field_guide.meaning: The high-level product identity and the explicit role of monitoring.
Sellable capability layers with role, purpose, user outcome, surfaces, assets, automation targets, learning signals, and validation gates.
Rules for what the first visible screen should emphasize.
How repeated work and accumulated data become prompts, workflows, templates, tools, skills, agents, or platform features.
Observable signals proving the platform is improving instead of only showing status.

product_position.primary_claim: A desktop platform for orchestrating agents, giving them a real work and development environment, making agents easier to create, and improving them through accumulated task, decision, evidence, validation, and evaluation data.

desktop_home_surface.home_copy_rule: The first screen should explain what the user can make agents do, create, and improve; observability appears as a support signal, not the headline.
desktop_home_surface.configuration_rule: Settings, setup, optional CLI configuration, and editor preferences belong to dedicated settings or capability surfaces rather than the top of the home view.

feature_layers.label: Agent Orchestration
feature_layers.purpose: Coordinate local/provider model tasks and optional CLI lanes as a supervised task graph with bounded IO, decision routing, merge gates, and cleanup.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user starts one task from chat and the platform runs the selected local/provider model or specialized lanes, pauses only dependent decisions, and keeps independent work moving.
automation_targets: direct model task execution from local Ollama models or connected OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini accounts
native local model catalog refresh through list_provider_models
provider credential injection into guest CLI sessions
AgentCore-style blueprint to native agent proposal creation
local Python agent execution with remote services treated as tool connectors
production agent blueprint selection for runtime, memory, gateway, and evaluation patterns
validation_gates: search agent work-chat exposes research-insight-planner-agent
local/provider models can produce task-run records without requiring a shell command
readiness test includes product feature architecture
resource guard covers long-running lanes
customer snapshot preserves feature claims without internal source
Agents screen exposes AgentCore-style production blueprint controls
Applying a production blueprint fills Search Agent Work Chat and Agent Factory inputs
Creating an AgentCore-style proposal uses the native Agent Factory proposal writer

feature_layers.label: Agent Work Environment
feature_layers.purpose: Host app-selected workspaces, runtime data stores, task-run records, decisions, support diagnostics, and agent work planes.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user no longer has to manually clone and work from a terminal-first folder; the app owns workspace selection and accumulated data access.
validation_gates: workspace boundary commands reject unsafe paths
accumulated data manifest is persisted
customer bundle excludes platform source

feature_layers.label: Agent Development Environment
feature_layers.purpose: Provide the developer workbench for source review, multi-file edits, diffs, templates, requirements, specs, validation, and runtime contracts.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can shape agent platform behavior inside a desktop workbench instead of bouncing between loose files and terminal-only flows.
validation_gates: Monaco code workbench is not only an embed
file writes stay within workspace root
requirements and specs trace product feature changes

feature_layers.label: Agent Factory
feature_layers.purpose: Turn repeated work into prompts, workflows, templates, tools, skills, agents, and finally platform features with traceable decisions.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can create agents and reusable capabilities without repeatedly telling the assistant the same process.
learning_signals: agent proposal saved from AgentCore-style blueprint
validation_gates: candidate has source evidence and rollback plan
skill or agent validation passes
promotion selects the smallest useful asset first
Agent Factory can be prefilled from a selected production blueprint
AgentCore Quick Builder can call the native agent proposal writer from the selected blueprint

feature_layers.label: Learning & Evaluation Loop
feature_layers.purpose: Accumulate work history, timing, evaluations, web searches, intent maps, evidence, and improvement records so platform behavior gets better over time.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can see why the platform improved, what evidence drove changes, and which gaps remain.
validation_gates: intent maps show source freshness
evaluations cite validation outcomes
new product work creates request trace and work summary

feature_layers.label: Observability & Monitoring
feature_layers.purpose: Expose structure, history, documents, source inventory, diagnostics, and status so the primary agent platform features can be understood and trusted.
feature_layers.user_outcome: The user can inspect accumulated data and platform state without mistaking that inspection layer for the whole product.
validation_gates: observability role remains supporting
customer snapshot removes internal source
readiness scripts check supporting role

promotion_loop.improvement_rule: When repeated human work, agent failures, omitted steps, validation failures, or useful patterns recur, create the smallest durable asset first and promote only when evidence justifies a larger feature.

quality_signals: The first screen names primary agent platform features before observability.
Snapshot data includes product feature architecture for developer and customer builds.
Customer snapshot preserves sellable feature structure but removes internal source paths and validation internals.
Readiness tests fail if monitoring is positioned as the primary product.
New feature work updates requirements, specs, validation, history, and request traces.
AgentCore-style blueprint choices map reference samples to runnable local product flows.
AWS deployment remains optional; the installed desktop app owns task state and accumulated records.

validation_gates.validates: Product feature registry keeps agent capability platform as the primary product and monitoring as supporting observability.
Workspace snapshot collector exposes product feature architecture and customer snapshot sanitization.
Customer bundle keeps product feature structure while stripping internal documents, source files, and implementation-only paths.

validation_gates.command: cd agent-platform && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m agent_platform.cli check-config-contract ../platform-desktop-app/configs/product-feature-registry.json

validation_gates.validates: Agents UI and product registries expose AgentCore-style production blueprints and quick proposal creation without making AWS mandatory.
